sectors.implications: Higher discount rates pressure long-duration equities (tech, growth); mortgage rates above 7% stress housing; duration risk is the dominant macro factor

Reduce exposure to mortgage REITs and homebuilders; favor rental/operating REITs; monitor delinquency data
Underweight French sovereigns and equities; favor German and Nordic exposure; monitor CDS spreads
Diversify beyond mega-cap AI; monitor Big Tech free cash flow vs. capex; watch for any capex pullback signal
The 2-month extension is temporary; prepare for potential tariff re-escalation; favor domestic-supply-chain equities

market_outlook.short_term: High volatility expected. Bond yields near 20-year highs and oil above $100 create a stagflationary pressure. S&P 500 showed intraday resilience on Hormuz deal hopes but remains vulnerable to any geopolitical escalation. Yen intervention risk and France political instability add noise. Expect range-bound equities with sharp intraday swings. Key: watch 30-year yield and oil as leading indicators.
market_outlook.long_term: AI capex cycle (Big Tech FCF tripling to $2T) supports structural tech growth, but AI leaders' catastrophe warnings and US/China policy divergence create uncertainty. India's market liberalization and defense spending provide secular tailwinds. Housing correction risk from 7%+ rates is a 6-12 month overhang. US-China trade truce is temporary; tariff re-escalation risk by late 2026. Bond market normalization will be the dominant long-term theme.
